meta.status: W-04 is ADDRESSED-GATED. Three official parcel-level lookups are specified and their instruments are linked. All three return blank because they require an address, which is withheld under the privacy rule.
meta.honesty_rule: No hazard zone is asserted for this parcel. A regional statement such as 'Los Angeles is seismically active' is TRUE and USELESS for pricing. It is recorded below as context only and is explicitly not a parcel finding.

context_only_not_parcel_findings.statement: Los Angeles County lies within a region of high seismic hazard, and the current national reference is the USGS 2023 50-state National Seismic Hazard Model.
context_only_not_parcel_findings.label: context
context_only_not_parcel_findings.not_a_finding: This says nothing about the parcel's shaking value, soil class, fault distance or liquefaction status.

context_only_not_parcel_findings.statement: CAL FIRE classifies lands into Moderate, High and Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones, and states that FHSZ maps measure hazard over a 30 to 50 year horizon and not risk.
context_only_not_parcel_findings.label: context
context_only_not_parcel_findings.not_a_finding: An urban parcel in Central LA is likely in a Local Responsibility Area rather than the State Responsibility Area, and LRA maps are released jurisdiction by jurisdiction. The parcel's class is unknown.

context_only_not_parcel_findings.statement: FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer is the authoritative current effective flood hazard database for NFIP purposes and covers over 90% of the U.S. population.
context_only_not_parcel_findings.label: context
context_only_not_parcel_findings.not_a_finding: The parcel's flood zone is unknown.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: California Geological Survey EQ Zapp (Seismic Hazards Mapping Act zones)
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: Liquefaction potential drives foundation and structural retrofit cost. A retrofit bill arriving in the 2030-2035 window lands either on the owner (as landlord repair obligation) or triggers a tenant termination right. Either way it is a direct hit to sale value.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: Enter [STREET-ADDRESS] in EQ Zapp and record the zone status verbatim. Note that the tool also reports when CGS has NOT evaluated the area, which is itself a finding.
Same lookup as HZ-01; record both the landslide and liquefaction determinations.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: California Geological Survey EQ Zapp / Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zone maps
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: A fault-rupture zone designation can preclude rebuild in kind after a loss, which converts a property insurance claim into a land-value-only outcome.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: EQ Zapp, and confirm against the published Alquist-Priolo zone map for the quadrangle.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: USGS National Seismic Hazard Model / Earthquake Hazard Toolbox
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: Design-basis shaking plus building code vintage sets the probable maximum loss (PML), which sets the insurance premium and the deductible the owner actually carries.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: Query the Toolbox at the parcel coordinates for the 2% in 50 year and 10% in 50 year values; pair with the year built from [SITE-PLAN].

parcel_screening.official_instrument: FEMA Flood Map Service Center / NFHL Viewer; FIRMette for the parcel
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: A Special Flood Hazard Area designation triggers mandatory flood insurance for any lender, and a Zone AE base flood elevation can force elevation or flood-proofing work on any re-let or remodel.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: Search [STREET-ADDRESS] on the MSC, download the FIRMette and record the zone, panel number and effective date verbatim.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: CAL FIRE / Office of the State Fire Marshal FHSZ viewer and zone lookup
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: For an urban Central LA parcel the fire question is less about wildfire than about whether an FHSZ designation would attach building-hardening requirements to any rebuild, and whether the property sits in an area insurers are withdrawing from.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: FHSZ lookup by address. If the parcel is in a Local Responsibility Area, obtain the local jurisdiction's adopted LRA map - CAL FIRE notes that LRA maps are released to jurisdictions, so the City is the authority.

parcel_screening.hazard: Wildfire history within the surrounding reporting area
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: CAL FIRE publishes historical perimeter GIS data; intersect with a 5 mile ring around the parcel. Record the most recent perimeter year and distance.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: Property condition assessment (PCA) and, if seismic retrofit is plausible, a seismic assessment
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: In a ground lease the box reverts to the owner at expiry in whatever condition the lease allows. The reversion value - often the largest single cash flow in the hold case - is a direct function of this number.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: Commission an ASTM-standard PCA from a licensed engineer. Keep it offline with authorised advisers.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: Certificate of insurance from [INSURANCE-POLICY] plus three broker indications
parcel_screening.why_it_changes_the_decision: California property insurance availability has become a binding constraint on transactions. A buyer will underwrite the insurance line, and an uninsurable building is a land sale.
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: Obtain the current certificate, the loss runs, and three written indications for a like-for-like renewal. Keep offline.

parcel_screening.official_instrument: CalEnviroScreen (CalEPA) and a Phase I ESA
parcel_screening.how_to_obtain: Look up the tract in CalEnviroScreen for the pollution-burden percentile, and commission a Phase I ESA before marketing. A QSR site carries historical fuel/degreaser risk.

stress_test_design.purpose: R-17 requires seismic, flood and fire to be stressed together with loss of rent, repairs and exit liquidity - not as three separate footnotes.

mechanics.driver: Months from event to rent resumption, times monthly rent
mechanics.note: In a NNN lease confirmed by HZ-05 style findings the tenant may still owe rent while closed - check the lease, do not assume.

mechanics.driver: Repair cost not covered by insurance, i.e. the deductible plus uninsured exclusions plus code-upgrade cost
mechanics.note: Older buildings commonly face code-triggered upgrade obligations after a loss.

mechanics.driver: Probability that a buyer will transact at all in the 12 months after an event
mechanics.note: This is the leg owners forget. After a regional event, transaction volume in the affected submarket goes to near zero for an extended period, so the owner cannot sell to avoid the other two legs.

stress_test_design.why_together: The three legs are correlated, not independent. A regional seismic event simultaneously stops rent, triggers repair obligations and closes the transaction market. Treating them as independent understates the tail by a wide margin.
